1.why: Verify compares the submitted token’s SHA-256 digest to session.recovery.tokenDigest with safeEqual, so only the session that received that token can use it.

2.why: Each recovery token is stored only on one session record; another session has no matching digest, so the same code does not work for other users.

3.why: Password change only sets session.passwordHash on the current session and never deletes or invalidates other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and non-HTTPS requests are rejected, but the code does not pin an explicit latest TLS version.

5.why: Passwords use bcrypt and reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests, but the MFA code is kept plaintext in session and nothing is encrypted at rest beyond hashing.

6.why: No real email is sent; API copy is generic and contact is never embedded, though the evaluation response does return testResetToken to the client.

7.why: Contact is not stored or reflected, passwords are hashed server-side, dynamic HTML uses escapeHtml, and the SPA inserts text only via textContent.

8.why: Client navigation uses only same-page hash routes and there is no open-redirect parameter or external redirect logic.

9.why: There are no email templates that interpolate user input; simulated delivery is plain text in the local logs panel.

10.why: Error JSON is generic, but testResetToken and testMfaCode are returned in API responses and written into the visible #logs panel and console.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in session memory, yet the MFA secret is hardcoded as session.mfaCode = "482913" in source.

12.why: No default usernames/passwords or built-in credential pairs are defined or accepted by the recovery flow.

13.why: Both per-session throttled() and trusted-IP ipThrottled() limit recovery, token, password, and MFA attempts and return 429 when exceeded.

14.why: The request endpoint always returns the same conditional message and never indicates whether the contact exists.

15.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte values from randomBytes (base64url), stored only as a per-session digest with TTL and single-use flags.
